prize_parts.citation: for discoveries concerning the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep a single-part B034 prize naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and my configuration is unchanged. The six round-1 statements agree on everything that bears on scientific merit and maturity: the chain from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect to the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, receptor biology and long-acting agonists is original and independently confirmed, and the outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease leave no timing question. The only open matter is framing, and I think the discovery framing is the stronger one. A prize recognises a discovery that visibly changed the field, and the discovery is the physiology and the active form of the hormone; the drugs are the proof that it matters, and the citation can say so ('made incretin-based therapies possible') without making a drug-development achievement the object of the prize. A two-part prize does not improve on this: it would cut the GLP-1 credit to two names and force a choice between discoverers, to add a basic or cell-therapy part that is less mature in medical impact.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point and I cannot remove it. Habener's group has a contested claim on the active peptide, he is outside the credited names, and a three-name cut omits Knudsen, whose analogue engineering put the biology into patients. I also have to concede that my own case rests on the supplied credit list and on literature I cannot audit against primary records here; if the documentary record showed that Mojsov's identification of the active form could not be sustained as distinct from Habener's, my configuration would be fragile and I would have to reconsider the third name. If B034 cannot reach a majority on an exact three-name set, B003 is my first fallback for its clean two-person attribution and very mature basic science, with the cost that its disease-translation record is only partial and the integrated stress response and the PERK and ATF6 branches are hard to separate from the core story. B040 is behind it because the omission of Eshhar and other early chimeric-receptor originators, and the Rosenberg credit, make a June, Sadelain and Rosenberg prize difficult to defend.

responses.point: The chair's configuration names Knudsen as third laureate with a citation covering the physiology of GLP-1 and the development of long-acting therapies, and he accepts that this honours industrial drug development.
responses.response: I have reconsidered this seriously, because the chair is right that a three-name prize leaves out either a discoverer or the person who turned a short-lived hormone into a usable drug. I still come out on the discovery side. Knudsen's work is optimisation of a peptide whose active form and actions had already been identified by others, and naming her makes the prize about development, which the committee would then have to defend against other industrial contributors with similar claims. The citation can acknowledge the therapies in its wording without crediting the development. The attribution wording matters as much as the name, so I would not object if the committee made the citation explicit that long-acting agonists are the consequence. We continue to differ on the third name, and I would only move if a priority review made Mojsov's claim unsustainable.

responses.point: El Manira would substitute Knudsen for Mojsov if a priority review showed her claim could not be sustained, but not on public controversy alone, and he would not combine B003 with B034 because that would cut the GLP-1 credit to two names.
responses.response: I agree on both points. A substitution should follow from the primary record on who identified and characterised the active GLP-1(7-36) amide, not from the existence of a dispute, and I accept that if it came to that, Knudsen is a more defensible replacement than a name outside the shortlist, since no one proposes Habener and his name is not credited on the ballot. I also share the objection to a two-part prize: pairing B003 with B034 would remove one of the three GLP-1 discoverers to make room for a part that is a different kind of achievement, and neither part would be improved by the trade.

responses.point: Linnarsson names Drucker, Holst and Mojsov with a citation on physiology and the active form, says a discovery-centred trio is the tradition of the prize, and lists B003 and B040 as alternatives while questioning whether the CAR-T priority questions can be resolved.
responses.response: We hold the same configuration, so the useful question is what would change it. On the CAR-T issue I think the answer is no: the omission of Eshhar and the early chimeric-receptor work is not something the committee can repair within a three-name limit, and B040 stays behind B003. I would add one limit to your wording: the citation should say 'active form' and not claim that Mojsov alone established it, since the record is shared with others. That keeps the citation accurate on what the committee can actually support.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius calls B034 arguably overdue, names the same trio, and says that if the active-peptide discovery cannot be assigned cleanly, a B034-centred prize would be fragile and B003 is the safer alternative.
responses.response: I agree that B003 is the right fallback and that the fragility is real, but I would separate two things. A contested priority claim does not make the prize unsafe; it makes the citation wording important. The citation should describe the discovery as the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form without asserting a single originator of the peptide identification. I am less convinced the work is overdue in a way that should affect the vote; the evidence for maturity is sufficient without that argument.

uncertainties: Whether the primary record supports crediting Mojsov for the identification of the active GLP-1 peptide as distinct from Habener's group; I cannot resolve this from the supplied evidence and am relying on literature recollection.
Whether the committee will accept a discovery-framed citation that mentions the therapies only as a consequence, or whether a majority needs Knudsen named to feel the prize covers the medicine.
Whether B003 or B040 is the better second choice if B034 stalls; I prefer B003 but its clinical translation is partial.
Whether the long-term safety questions raised for incretin therapy would affect the maturity assessment; I regard them as not decisive.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My earlier disclosures stand: a Salk-period nuclear-receptor collaboration with Ronald Evans, past co-authorship with Per Svenningsson (dopamine neurons, Nurr1) and a 2009 paper with Abdel El Manira. None of these people is credited on the shortlist, so I see no recusal need.
